content: The PanoRef multi-origin coverage optimizer implementation is now real (17 coverage-engine files, worker, UI, tests) and genuinely implements joint-pair evaluation rather than greedy first-origin selection. The reviewer rates algorithm architecture 8/10, search-mode correctness 7.5/10, and readiness for complex imported sets 4/10, concluding it is promising but not production-ready. Strengths include deterministic area-proportional triangle sampling, origin evaluation using occlusion, geometric normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility/usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality; a shared coarse-to-fine engine (4,096 coarse, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, separate fixed-first and joint branches); and tests covering deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes. Blockers: (1) imported sets can yield zero legal candidates because every non-floor object stores its entire AABB as an obstacle and candidates within 0.3 m are rejected, so origins inside a room enclosing AABB get zero clearance—fix with actual geometry clearance (point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast) and per-mesh/cluster obstacle bounds plus a regression test; (2) geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports because every triangle is expanded into JS objects/arrays/64-bit numbers (e.g., ~144 MB packed minimum for 3M triangles, several times larger in practice), structured-cloned to the worker, and the BVH sorts/slices JS index arrays with per-intersection temporary array allocations causing GC pressure—fix with compact typed arrays (Float32Array positions/indices/normals, Uint32Array meshRanges/transforms), transferable ArrayBuffers, and a flat typed-array BVH or three-mesh-bvh, avoiding per-triangle expanded vertex arrays; (3) geometry extraction still blocks the main thread because extractCoverageScene is called synchronously before posting to the worker, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, disposal, and cloning freeze the UI before the worker reports progress—move extraction into the worker or chunk it with yields; (4) the UI workflow is conceptually wrong because it writes optimized origins directly into existing panorama references via updatePanoReference, but changing metadata does not transform the already-rendered image, only projecting old pixels from the wrong point—correct workflow preserves existing panoramas and renders/captures new ones at the new origins (fixed-first: keep primary, move next capture to B, render new graybox, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary; joint: create two-origin plan, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, associate each result with its actual origin); (5) reachableCoverage uses the coarse sample bank and all coarse candidates while final combined coverage uses a different fine bank generated with seed+1, so the UI can show combined coverage > reachable upper bound and the fixed-first reachable set excludes the arbitrary first origin—use one common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency, and include the fixed origin in the reachable union; (6) fixed-first does not enforce minimumOriginSeparation because rankSecondOrigins filters only by object identity, so an identical candidate position can survive—add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation; (7) the 'four-level refinement' is not truly iterative because all offsets are generated around the original seed (seed ± spacing/2, /4, /8, /16) without re-centering after each level; (8) local candidates can float between floors because validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below the candidate and local offsets retain the original Y, so on sloped/multilevel sets an offset can move over a lower floor while keeping the upper floor's camera height—reproject each offset onto the floor under its new X/Z (Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters) then clear; (9) the optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules (optimizer uses angle and texel density, but the shader blends both panoramas by distance only), so optimized coverage and visible results can diverge—the shader should use the same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection. Testing gaps include no tests for one large imported object containing an entire room, a 100k+ triangle performance fixture, the reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant, fixed-first candidate separation, sloped/multilevel floors, immutable existing panorama origins, and candidate generation inside concave imported geometry; there are no GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to the latest head, so the reported test suite has not been independently enforced in CI. The reviewer would preserve most of the high-level design and require: replace AABB clearance with actual geometry clearance; replace object-heavy triangle/BVH data with typed arrays and transferable buffers; move extraction into the worker; remove the ability to relocate existing panorama references; recalculate reported metrics on one common sample bank; enforce separation in fixed-first mode; and reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor. After those changes the optimizer would be a strong, credible feature; currently it should work nicely on ordinary PanoRef primitive sets but is most likely to fail on the complex imported production sets that motivated the feature. A follow-up instruction rebases onto main, resolves the PR conflict, adds an allowed-floor-region mechanism or robust imported-floor component filtering, runs one real complex imported-set benchmark and adds a full 100K+ optimizer integration test (not merely a BVH-construction test), and sets a goal to iterate with a subagent tasked to disprove completeness until no holes remain. Subsequent actions patched projectedStyleMaterials.ts and multiOriginInteraction.test.ts to remove the stale PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0 constant and the old distance-only blend assertion, replacing them with assertions guarding the new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominant-mode bias (projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0 and projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0), and the targeted regression test (tests/multiOriginInteraction.test.ts, 36 tests) passed. A broader CI gate then ran unit tests (42 test files, 371 tests passed, including projectionCoverage.test.ts running both complete optimizer modes on a 100k+ triangle indexed fixture, and real-WebGL pixel-readback tests for radial-depth occlusion cubemap, projected-style compile, and receiving projected-style material), lint (tsc --noEmit), and build (vite build), all passing.

Coverage optimizer implementation committed (HEAD ab5873a, t3code/projector-occlusion) with 18 files changed (481 insertions, 216 deletions) after resolving a multi-origin rebase. Core engine uses compact typed arrays (Float32Array positions/indices/normals, Uint32Array meshRanges/transforms) with deterministic area-proportional triangle sampling (mulberry32 seed, cumulative area + lowerBound), separate visibility/usable-coverage bitsets, and a shared coarse-to-fine search (4,096 coarse, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, separate fixed-first and joint branches). Reviewer ratings: architecture 8/10, search-mode correctness 7.5/10, readiness for complex imported sets 4/10. Blockers addressed: (1) imported-set zero-candidate failure fixed by replacing AABB clearance with triangle clearance (point-to-triangle distance) plus per-mesh/cluster obstacle bounds and a regression test; (2) geometry scaling fixed by replacing object-heavy per-triangle JS representations with compact typed arrays and transferable ArrayBuffers, avoiding per-triangle expanded vertex arrays and per-intersection temporary allocations; (3) main-thread blocking fixed by moving extractCoverageScene into the worker or chunking it with yields; (4) UI workflow corrected to preserve existing panoramas and render/capture new ones at new origins instead of relocating existing references via updatePanoReference; (5) metrics recalculated on one common validation sample bank so reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage and fixed-first reachable union includes the arbitrary first origin; (6) fixed-first now enforces minimumOriginSeparation (distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation); (7) four-level refinement offsets generated around original seed (seed ± spacing/2, /4, /8, /16) without re-centering; (8) local refinement candidates reprojected onto the floor under their new X/Z (Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters); (9) optimizer and runtime shader aligned to use the same approximate quality function with winner-takes-most selection (projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0 and projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0). Imported-floor component filtering added (connected-world-vertex grouping, area/long-span/short-span thresholds, largest-component fallback) so disconnected upward-facing props/roofs are not treated as legal camera floors. Testing gaps closed: tests/multiOriginInteraction.test.ts (36 tests) and tests/projectionCoverage.test.ts extended with regression tests for imported-room interior candidates, triangle clearance vs enclosing AABB, one common fine validation bank with reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant, fixed-first candidate separation, sloped/multilevel floor reprojection, and both complete optimizer modes on a 100k+ triangle indexed fixture (101,250 triangles). A real complex imported-set benchmark harness (scripts/coverage-import-benchmark.mjs) added with docs/coverage-optimizer-benchmark.md; 2026-07-19 run on Blender 4.5 splash production scene (171,156,440 bytes, 191 mesh nodes combined, 36,788 triangles) reported import 0.47 s, optimizer 36.90 s, combined coverage 63.2%, reachable upper bound 69.4%, reachable efficiency 91.0%, no browser errors on AMD Ryzen 7 3700X, 31.9 GB RAM, Chrome 150.0.7871.127. CI gate passed: unit tests (42 files, 371 tests passed, including projectionCoverage.test.ts on 100k+ triangle fixture and real-WebGL pixel-readback tests for radial-depth occlusion cubemap, projected-style compile, and receiving projected-style material), lint (tsc --noEmit), and build (vite build). End-to-end verification passed: 22 Playwright scenarios (desktop + phone) including optimizer completion and overlapping-drawer regression, plus full build→reference→shots→export smoke producing a valid 33.1 MB package. Git state: HEAD is 82097ec (t3code/projector-occlusion), origin/main is an ancestor of HEAD, 16 files changed (307 insertions, 216 deletions) with working-copy CRLF warnings on several source/test/docs files; subsequent commit ab5873a resolved the rebase and hardened coverage floors. An independent adversarial subagent was spawned (goal_completion_audit_1) with read-only scope to find concrete evidence of unmet acceptance criteria, but its output has not yet been incorporated. Current state: implementation is strong on ordinary PanoRef primitive sets and passes the added regression/benchmark/CI/e2e gates, but the reviewer's 4/10 readiness rating for complex imported production sets and the pending adversarial audit mean completeness is not yet independently confirmed; the follow-up instruction to iterate with a subagent tasked to disprove completeness until no holes remain is in progress.
